title: How to change your phone number: Steps by carrier for Android and iPhone
summary: Here’s how to change a phone number with T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T, then update 2FA, Google, and your other accounts so you don't get locked out.
body_markdown:
It’s time to break up with your old phone number. Maybe you’re trying to keep your personal and business numbers separate. Maybe you’re moving and need a new area code. Or maybe you’re just tired of spam calls and mystery voicemails from your number’s previous owner.


Well, switching your phone number is easier than you think.


This guide explains how to change a phone number on Android and iOS devices. Plus, if you’re a business, we’ll show you why a[VoIP app](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-voip-app/) may be the smarter move.


##


**How to change your phone number with your carrier**


Most major service providers handle mobile number changes through their app or website, so the exact steps and fees vary by carrier.


Here’s a summary of what you can expect:


Carrier Where you change your number Fee How long it takes


T-Mobile T-Life app or T-Mobile.com Free twice a year, with a limit of one change per month. Otherwise, it costs $15 per change. Up to four hours. iMessage can take up to 24 hours to update. Logging in to your account at T-mobile.com with the new number can take up to three days.


Verizon My Verizon app or website, or by calling customer service Free in the app or online. $15 if you call. Immediately if you choose today. Otherwise, it changes at midnight ET on the date you pick.


AT&T Your online wireless account, an AT&T store, or by contacting AT&T Free within 30 days of activation. $36 after that. Not stated on AT&T’s site.


**⚠️Watch out:** Before you change your


phone number


, move


two-factor authentication


from texts to an authenticator app where possible. Also consider saving


voicemails


and exporting contacts and important


text messages


. That way, you don’t lose important information.


### **How to change a** **phone number** **with** **T-Mobile**


If you’re a primary account holder, you can change your T-Mobile number in two ways: through the app or the website. Here’s how:


**How to change your phone number** **through T-Life**


In the T-Life app:


1. Select the **Account** tab, then choose the number you want to change.
2. Select **Change** **phone number.**
3. Review the important information T-Mobile shows you, then choose **Acknowledge & continue.**
4. Enter your city and state or ZIP code you want, then select **Search** .
5. Pick an available number from up to five random ones and select **Continue** .
6. Review the details of your number change and click **Select** .


**How to change a** **phone number** **through** **T-Mobile** **’s site**


Sign in to your account on T-Mobile.com. Then:


1. Choose the number you want to change, then select **Change** **phone number** .
2. Review the warnings and important information, then choose **Acknowledge & continue** .
3. Confirm the number and select **Continue** .
4. Enter the city and state or ZIP code you want, then select **Search** .
5. Select one of the available numbers and then select **Continue** .
6. Review the details of the change and then select **Submit** .


According to[T-Mobile’s support page](https://www.t-mobile.com/support/account/change-your-phone-number) , you can change your number twice a year at no cost, with a limit of one change per month. If you want to change your number more often, T-Mobile charges a $15 fee per change.


The change can take up to four hours, and T-Mobile texts you the new number when it’s done. It also deletes your voicemail messages.


### **How to change a** **phone number** **with Verizon**


If you’re an account owner or account manager, you can change a Verizon number in the My Verizon app or on Verizon’s site.


Here’s how:


**How to change your phone number** **in the** **My Verizon app**


Open the My Verizon app and sign in. Then:


1. Tap the **Mobile tab** followed by **Manage devices** .
2. Tap **Device Management** , then **Change** **mobile number** .
3. Select the number you want to change, then select **Continue** and **Get a new number** .
4. Enter the five-digit ZIP code for your new number, then tap the **Down Arrow icon** to choose the first six digits of your new number.
5. Pick the date you want the change to take effect. Your number will change at midnight ET of that day. Choose today to get the new number right away. Then tap **Continue** .
6. Review the details and **Submit** the change.


**How to change a** **phone number** **on Verizon’s site**


Sign in at Verizon.com. Then:


1. Select **Account** , then **My devices** .
2. Choose **Change** **mobile number** and select the number you want to change.
3. Choose **Get a new number** .
4. Select your location by ZIP code. You can also choose by state or city.
5. Pick the first six digits of your new phone number from the options available.
6. Choose when you want the change to take effect, then click **Continue** .
7. Pick the last four digits of your number from the options Verizon gives you. Then click **Continue** .
8. Review the details and **Submit** the change.


Both of these methods are free. You can also call Verizon customer service to do it for you. However, that costs $15.


On the date you picked for the number change, Verizon suggests turning your device off and back on again. Then wait a few minutes for your phone to update. Once the number exchange is complete, anyone who calls your old number gets a message that it’s no longer in service.


### **How to change a** **phone number** **with AT&T**


You can change your AT&T number online, at an AT&T store, or by contacting their team. Here’s how to do it online:


1. Go to your wireless account and sign in.
2. Select **Switch** to choose a number.
3. Choose **Device** options, then **Change** **phone number** .
4. Complete the form and click **Search** to see the numbers you can choose from.
5. Pick the number you want, then follow the on-screen prompts to finish.


With AT&T, you can change your wireless number for free within 30 days of activating it. If you want to exchange your phone number after that period, there’s a $36 change fee. If you don’t see the option to change your number, check that the Wireless Account Lock setting is turned off.


##


**How to change the phone number on your cell phone device**


Now let’s look at how to change the phone number on your iOS or Android device:


### **How to change a** **phone number** **on an** **iPhone**


Here’s how to change your phone number on iOS:


1. Under **Settings** , tap on **Cellular** .


2. Tap **My Number** .


3. Type in your new number, including the country code, and tap **Save** .


4. Restart your phone to apply the changes.


Don’t forget to notify contacts that you’ve recently changed your number. You should also back up your data to iCloud to avoid communication breakdowns.


### **How to change your number on Android**


Here’s how to change the number on an Android phone:


1. Under Settings, tap **Google** or your name/profile.
2. Select **Manage your** **Google Account** .
3. Tap **Personal info** .
4. Tap **Phone** , then tap on your number.
5. Select the **Edit** , or pencil, icon next to your number. Google may ask you to verify your identity at this step.
6. Tap **Update number** and follow the on-screen instructions to enter your new number.


And that’s it — you’ve successfully changed your Android number.


Just make sure your new number is updated across your Google Accounts by refreshing the **Personal** **info** screen.

##


**Common issues when changing your** **phone number**


Here’s what to consider before switching your SIM card:


### **Two-factor authentication** **disruptions**


If you use your old number for verification codes, switching to a new phone number could lock you out of important accounts. Avoid the headache of account recovery by migrating your 2FA before switching:


- **Remove your old number from each account’s 2FA settings** . This includes banks, social media profiles, and subscriptions.
- **Add another method, like an authenticator app or backup codes** . These are one-time codes you can use to log in if you receive texts. Generate them in each account’s security settings and store them somewhere other than your phone.
- **Once your new number is active, add it to your 2FA settings** .


**Note: Most virtual numbers like Quo aren’t always accepted for 2FA. We recommend keeping a traditional cell* *phone number* *for verification purposes.*


### **Lost** **voicemails** **, texts, and call logs**


If your old number was with a carrier like T-Mobile or Verizon, switching[could wipe out voicemails](https://www.verizon.com/support/change-mobile-number-faqs/) , text messages, and call records. If those details aren’t backed up, they’ll be gone for good — not ideal for business owners.


### **Important contacts can’t reach you**


If customers don’t recognize your new number, they might not answer — meaning missed opportunities.


You’ve got a few options for keeping them posted:


- [Bulk import contacts](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/contacts/import#csv-file-import) **from your old number to your new number** . Then you can call or leave a message letting them know about the change.
- **Set up temporary**[call forwarding](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-forward-calls/) **to your new number** . This will help you avoid missing calls and opportunities during the transition.
- **Add your old and new numbers to the same device** . That way, you’ll receive calls from both and can sort out any issues without dropping important conversations.

##


**FAQs**


**Is it free to change your phone number?**


It depends on your carrier. T-Mobile lets you change your phone number twice a year for free. If you want to change your number more often, T-Mobile charges a $15 fee per change. Changing your number online with Verizon is also free, while calling their customer service to make the change costs $15. With AT&T, changing your number costs $36 if you do it more than 30 days after activation.
Changing your number with Quo is free beyond paying for the plan itself. Our business phone plans start at $15 per user per month.


**Will you lost your history if you change phone numbers?**


The information that’s stored on your phone stays. But if it’s tied to your number, voicemails and texting history, for example, will get deleted. On Quo, changing your number permanently removes the old number’s call and message history. So be sure to back up your information before switching numbers.


**What happens to your old phone number when you change numbers?**


Under[FCC rules](https://www.fcc.gov/reassigned-numbers-database) , carriers must wait at least 45 days after a number is permanently disconnected before giving it to someone else. After that, a new owner can receive it, so move your accounts off the old number first.


**How can you switch phone numbers for your Google account when using an Android tablet?**


Open Settings, tap **Google** , then tap your **Username** . Tap **Manage your** **Google Account** , followed by **Personal info** . Then tap **Phone** under Contact info, select your number, then tap **Edit** and **Update number** .


**What are the steps for updating your phone number on WhatsApp?**


Open WhatsApp on your phone and tap the vertical **…** on the top right. Go to **Settings, Account,** and **Change** **phone number** . Enter your old and new numbers, choose whether to notify your contacts, and enter the verification code WhatsApp sends. You can’t do this on WhatsApp Web or Desktop.


**Can I keep my number but change providers?**


Yes. Porting moves your existing number to a new provider, so you can switch carriers without changing it. It’s useful for a business number your customers already know. That’s because you can port that number out and then change your personal number without losing the business line. So[how long does porting take](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-long-does-it-take-to-port-a-number/) ? Switching between mobile providers can take minutes to hours, depending on the cell phone carrier. Moving to a virtual phone number provider like Quo typically takes five to seven business days for US numbers, and 10–12 days for Canadian numbers. Quo doesn’t charge for it, though your old carrier might.
To port a number into Quo:
1. Navigate to **Settings** and **Phone numbers** , then click **Port an existing number** . You need to be a workspace owner or admin.
2. Select your current carrier and enter the number you want to port.
3. Upload your billing information and a recent statement, then enter your carrier credentials.
4. Quo submits the request to your carrier and confirms the port date with you.
5. On the port date, the number becomes available in your Quo account. Cancel your old service only after the port is complete.
